root_cause.text: Off-by-one error in the cleanup loop of `setup_nic_devices()` where `while(i--)` decrements `i` before the loop body, causing the device at the failing index to be skipped and not freed, leading to a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the loop from `while(i--)` to `do { ... } while(i--)` and adds `i--` before the `devlink_alloc` failure goto to ensure the failing index is properly cleaned up. The commit message states: "The current cleanup loop while(i--) skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error path to properly adjust loop counter before cleanup on devlink allocation failure.
intent_record.what: Added a decrement of loop variable `i` before jumping to cleanup label when devlink allocation fails.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the cleanup routine only frees resources for previously allocated devices, avoiding attempts to free uninitialized or incorrectly freed memory for the device that just experienced an allocation failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug where NIC device cleanup would be skipped entirely if setup failed on the first device (i=0), by changing the cleanup loop from while to do-while to guarantee at least one iteration.
intent_record.what: Changed the loop in the error cleanup path from a pre-test while loop (while (i--)) to a post-test do-while loop (do { ... } while (i--)).
intent_record.how: The original while loop would skip the body entirely if the loop variable i was zero at entry, meaning no cleanup would be performed when setup fails on the first device (index 0). The do-while loop guarantees that the body executes at least once, even when i is zero, ensuring that the device at index 0 is cleaned up in such a failure scenario.
